reason: planning stopped before any code was written: the plan still needed revising in the last round (round 5 of 5). I read the code the plan names and checked its main claims. Most hold: SlotQueue::acquire/try_acquire/waiting/from_config, Class::Producer = 2, the flock-based slot files, the pre-commit/commit-msg dispatch at main.rs:551, policy.rs evaluate/check_bash/check_segment/check_cargo/tokenize and the `bash` helper at 991, invocation.rs invoke_and_record (the Invocation literal is in invocation_record at 195, plus interrupted_record at 281), reading.rs agent_spec with `side`, and procs kill_group/group_alive. Only run/producer.rs:166 passes Side::Produce, and every Policy literal outside policy.rs is a verifier policy, including tests/binary.rs:98. I found no reader of the changed code that the dependents list leaves out. The six 'outside the deliverables' findings in the brief are explained in decision 17: each file is either the only place that can do the job or a one-line edit needed to compile. One major gap: the policy lets the producer put global flags before the subcommand (`cargo -q build`, `cargo --locked test`; CARGO_GLOBAL_FLAGS at policy.rs:477-486), and the plan's own policy rule requires the wrapper for `cargo -q build`. But the plan never says how the wrapper finds the subcommand. `cargo_subcommand` is added to policy.rs as a private function, and the criterion 1 tests use only bare `cargo build/test/clippy/check`. A wrapper that looks only at its first argument would run these common forms with no slot, and no test would catch it. Three minor points: the hook checks its own PATH, not the one the Bash tool uses; the 'not failed' test cannot fail without the feature; and the peak is only sampled when a producer command wins a slot. Line references to three Invocation literals are slightly off (nit). Verdict: revise.
